frequency_question: What proportion of such attempts succeed within two years of initiation?
membership_rule: Includes any sovereign state receiving Western military aid that attempts to domesticate production of high-tech Western guided missiles or cruise missiles during an active conventional war.

cases.name: Ukraine domestic production attempts of Western 155mm artillery shells (Rheinmetall joint ventures)
Ukraine domestic adaptation of Neptune anti-ship missiles using foreign components
Ukraine attempt at domestic production of Western-standard air defense interceptors (FrankenSAM program)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named; represents the total population of direct peer analogs for high-tech defense industrial localization under active invasion in the 21st century.
known_gaps: SCALP/Storm Shadow is significantly more technologically complex than 155mm shells or FrankenSAM jury-rigged air defense, representing a material difference in technical friction.
skeleton: Three major defense-industrial adaptation initiatives under active wartime conditions; all three achieved functional domestic assembly or manufacturing lines within the two-year window, though differing in scale and technological complexity.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 3 relevant historical precedents for wartime PGM/heavy munitions localization.
validity_reason: Remains valid as long as the current paradigm of Western-Ukrainian defense-industrial integration and deep technological transfer persists.
